en: The Sūtra on the Prophecy of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva, translated by the Śramaṇa Dharmodgata of Huanglong Country during the Song Dynasty.
Thus have I heard: At one time, the Buddha was staying at the Deer Park of the Rishis in Vārāṇasī, together with...
There was a great assembly of twenty thousand bhikṣus and twelve thousand bodhisattvas. Their names were:

Bodhisattva Siṃha, Bodhisattva Siṃhamati, Bodhisattva Kṣemamati, Bodhisattva Anupamamati, Bodhisattva Dharaṇīdhara, Bodhisattva Prajñāda, Bodhisattva Devaśrī, Bodhisattva Tattvārtha, Bodhisattva Gahvara, Bodhisattva Bhadrabala, Bodhisattva Jñānadeva, Bodhisattva Priyadarśana, Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī, Bodhisattva Jñānacaryā, Bodhisattva Ekacaryā, Bodhisattva Vighuṣṭanirāvaraṇa, and Bodhisattva Maitreya. With these as their leaders, there were twelve thousand bodhisattva-mahāsattvas present together.
Furthermore, there were twenty thousand devaputras, with the devaputra Śubhakṛt and the devaputra Śubhasthita as their leaders, all of whom were established in the Mahāyāna.
At that time, the World-Honored One was surrounded by immeasurable hundreds of thousands of attendants as he preached the Dharma for them.

At that time, there was a bodhisattva in the assembly named Puṣpadharagarbha. He rose from his seat, bared his right shoulder, knelt with his right knee on the ground, joined his palms toward the Buddha, and spoke these words:
"I pray that the World-Honored One will grant me an interval, for I wish to ask a question."
The Buddha told the Bodhisattva Flower-Virtue-Treasury:
"Ask whatever you wish; all those who have doubts, I already know them, and I shall explain them for you so that you may be filled with joy."
At that time, Puṣpadharagarbha addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

How does a bodhisattva mahāsattva become non-retrogressive regarding anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi and the five supernormal powers, attain the illusion-like samādhi, and, through skillful means, manifest transformed bodies to preach the Dharma according to the various forms and classes of beings, based on the roots of goodness they have cultivated, so that they may attain anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi?”
The Buddha addressed the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Puṣpadharagarbha:
“Excellent! Excellent!”
That you are able to inquire about such a meaning before the Tathāgata, the Samyaksaṃbuddha— O Puṣpākara-garbha,

you have already planted roots of goodness under various Buddhas of the past, made offerings to countless hundreds of thousands of myriads of koṭis of Buddha-Bhagavāns, and given rise to great compassion for all sentient beings.
Excellent, Puṣpadeva-garbha!
Listen attentively!
Listen attentively!
Reflect upon it well!
I shall speak for you.
He replied, “Indeed! I wish most earnestly to hear it.”
The Buddha addressed the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Flower-Virtue-Treasury:
"By accomplishing one dharma, one attains the illusion-like samādhi.

Having attained this samādhi, through skillful means one can transform one's body; according to the types of forms of sentient beings and the roots of goodness they have cultivated, one preaches the Dharma for them, enabling them to attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi."
What is this one dharma?

It is non-reliance. One does not rely on the three realms, nor does one rely on the internal, nor does one rely on the external; thus, one attains right observation regarding that which has no basis for reliance.
Having practiced correct observation, one attains right exhaustion, yet there is no diminution in one's awareness.
With a mind free from decrease, one fully traverses right wisdom, realizing that all phenomena arise from conditions and exist only as provisional designations.
All phenomena arise from causes and conditions; if there were no causes and conditions, there would be no phenomena that arise.
Although all phenomena arise from causes and conditions, there is nothing that arises.

One who thus penetrates the dharma of non-arising attains entry into the true path of the bodhisattva; this is also called attaining entry into the mind of great compassion, out of pity seeking to deliver all sentient beings.
Having thoroughly and deeply understood this meaning, one then knows that all phenomena are like illusions, being merely the products of conceptualization and verbal expression.
Yet these phenomena produced by conceptualization and verbal expression are ultimately and entirely empty.
Having thoroughly mastered the emptiness of all phenomena, this is called attaining the Illusion-like Samādhi.

Having attained this samādhi, through skillful means he is able to transform his body, manifesting in accordance with the various forms and types of sentient beings to cultivate roots of goodness and preach the Dharma for them, enabling them to attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattva Padmaśrīgarbha addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!
Within this assembly, are there any bodhisattvas who have attained this samādhi?"
The Buddha said: "There are!
Within this very assembly, sixty virtuous men, including Maitreya Bodhisattva and Mañjuśrī, have adorned themselves with inconceivable great vows and have attained this samādhi."
Again, he addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
Is it only the bodhisattvas of this world who attain this samādhi? Or are there also bodhisattvas in other worlds who have accomplished such an illusion-like samādhi?”
The Buddha told Puṣpacitra:

"To the west, beyond hundreds of thousands of millions of buddha-fields, there is a world named Sukhāvatī. In that land there is a Buddha, titled Amitābha Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, who is currently residing and preaching the Dharma."
In that land there are two bodhisattvas: the first is named Avalokiteśvara and the second is named Mahāsthāmaprāpta;
they have attained this samādhi. Furthermore, Puṣpakuṭi!
If there is a bodhisattva who, for seven days and seven nights, listens to and receives this Dharma from those noble beings, they will immediately attain the illusion-like samādhi (māyopama-samādhi).
The Bodhisattva Puṣpadharagarbha addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
In that land, there must be immeasurable bodhisattvas who have attained this samādhi.”
"Why is this? Because all other bodhisattvas born in that land shall go to where that true person (satpuruṣa) resides to hear and receive this Dharma.
The Buddha said:
"So it is! So it is! It is just as you have said."
“There are immeasurable, asaṃkhyeya bodhisattva-mahāsattvas who have obtained this samādhi from that noble being.
The Bodhisattva Puṣpakuṭidhara addressed the Buddha,
saying, “Excellent!”
World-Honored One, Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha!
We pray that by your supernatural power, you will cause that noble son to arrive in this world, so that both he and we may see one another.

Why is this? Because those true beings have arrived in this land, sons and daughters of good family who have cultivated roots of goodness, upon hearing their preaching of the Dharma, shall attain this samādhi;

furthermore, they shall wish to see Amitābha Buddha in that Land of Peace and Bliss, causing these sons and daughters of good family to resolve their minds toward *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* and vow to be born in that realm.
"Once born in that land, they shall never again regress from *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.

At that time, having accepted their request, the World-Honored One emitted a ray of light from the white tuft of hair between his eyebrows, which illuminated the entire trichiliocosm. Within this world, the grasses, trees, earth, stones, Mount Sumeru, King Mucilinda Mountain, Mahāmucilinda Mountain, Cakravāḍa Mountains, and Mahācakravāḍa Mountains—even the dark and obscure places between worlds—were all universally turned golden, such that there was no place not brightly illumined.
The radiance of the sun and moon, as well as the majestic power and light of great beings, no longer appeared at all.
The entire Western direction—extending through hundreds of thousands of millions of lands up to the world of Sukhāvatī—was entirely the color of gold.
Mahāprabha circumambulated that Buddha seven times to the right and then vanished from before the Tathāgata.

The sentient beings, bodhisattvas, and śrāvakas of that land all saw this world, as well as Śākyamuni surrounded by his great assembly preaching the Dharma, as clearly as if they were looking at an āmalaka fruit in the palm of their hand. They all conceived feelings of love, joy, and delight, and cried out these words:
“Namo to Śākyamuni Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha!”

In this assembly—comprising bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, upāsikās, devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, humans and non-humans, as well as Śakra, Brahmā, the Four Great Kings, bodhisattvas, and śrāvakas—all beheld the Buddha Amitābha of the Land of Peace and Bliss, surrounded by a retinue of bodhisattvas and śrāvakas. He was resplendent like a mountain of jewels, towering and extraordinary; his majestic light blazed forth, illuminating all buddha-fields, just as a person with clear vision perceives the features of another’s face within a fathom’s distance with perfect clarity and without obstruction.
Having seen this, they were filled with joy and leaped for gladness, crying out these words:
"Namo to the Tathāgata Amitābha, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha."
At that time, eighty-four thousand beings within this assembly all resolved their minds upon Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, planted roots of goodness, and made vows to be born in that land.

At that time, the bodhisattvas and śrāvakas of the world Sukhāvatī, having seen this land, marveled at such an unprecedented occurrence. With joy, they joined their palms, paid homage to the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Śākyamuni, and spoke these words:
“Namo to Śākyamuni Buddha! You are able to preach such a Dharma for the sake of bodhisattvas and śrāvakas!”

At that time, the world of Sukhāvatī shook in six ways: it quaked, quaked everywhere, and quaked equally everywhere; it trembled, trembled everywhere, and trembled equally everywhere; it rattled, rattled everywhere, and rattled equally everywhere.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas Avalokiteśvara and Mahāsthāmaprāpta addressed that Buddha, saying:
“How extraordinary, World-Honored One!
The Tathāgata Śākyamuni has manifested a rare and wondrous feat.”
Why is this? Because that Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Śākyamuni has manifested his name but briefly, yet it has caused the great earth of the non-conceptual realm to quake in six ways.
At that time, Amitābha Buddha addressed those bodhisattvas:
"Śākyamuni does not manifest his name only in this land; he manifests his name in all the other immeasurable buddha-worlds as well."
A great light shone everywhere and the earth shook in six ways; it was likewise so for those worlds.

Immeasurable *asaṃkhyeya* sentient beings in those worlds, upon hearing the praise of the name of Śākyamuni, perfected their roots of goodness and all attained non-retrogression from *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.

At that time, four billion bodhisattvas within that assembly, upon hearing the name of the Tathāgata Śākyamuni—the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha—united their voices in making vows and dedicated their roots of goodness toward anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
The Buddha then bestowed upon them the prophecy that they would attain anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.

At that time, the Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas Avalokiteśvara and Mahāsthāmaprāpta went to where that Buddha was, prostrated themselves at his feet with their heads, joined their palms in reverence, stood to one side, and addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!”
“By what cause and by what condition has Śākyamuni emitted this radiance?
At that time, that Buddha told Avalokiteśvara:
“The Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, has emitted this radiance for no reason other than a specific cause and condition.”
Why is this? Because today the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Śākyamuni is about to expound the *Bodhisattvamaṇigocarasthitisamādhi Sūtra*, and therefore he first manifests these auspicious omens.
At that time, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas Avalokiteśvara and Mahāsthāmaprāpta addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
We wish to go to the Sahā world to pay homage to and make offerings to Śākyamuni Buddha, and to listen to his preaching of the Dharma.”
The Buddha said,
"Good son, you should know that now is the time."
Then, the two bodhisattvas said to one another,
"Today we shall certainly hear the sublime Dharma spoken by that Buddha.
Having received the Buddha's instruction, the two bodhisattvas addressed their retinue of four billion bodhisattvas:
“Good son! We should go together to the Sahā world to pay homage and make offerings to Śākyamuni Buddha, and to hear and receive the True Dharma. Why is this?

The Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha Śākyamuni is able to perform what is difficult to do: having relinquished a pure and wondrous land, by the power of his original vows and giving rise to great compassion, he attained Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi and preached the Dharma within this turbid and evil world of meager virtue and merit, where greed, anger, and delusion abound.
When these words were spoken, the bodhisattvas and śrāvakas raised their voices in unison and exclaimed:

"The sentient beings of that land who hear the name of the Tathāgata Śākyamuni—Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha—have gained a swift and great benefit; how much more so for those who actually see him and give rise to a heart of joy!"
“World-Honored One!
We shall go together to that world to pay homage to and make offerings to Śākyamuni Buddha.
The Buddha said:
“Good son! You should know that now is the time.

At that moment, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas Avalokiteśvara and Mahāsthāmaprāpta, surrounded by forty billion bodhisattvas before and behind them, used their supernormal powers to manifest forty billion adorned jewel terraces for their retinues within that world.
These jeweled terraces were twelve *yojanas* in length and breadth, exquisite and sublime.

Upon these terraces, some places were of gold, some of silver, some of lapis lazuli, some of crystal, some of red pearls, some of musaragalva, and some of agate. Some places consisted of two jewels—gold and silver; some of three jewels—gold, silver, and lapis lazuli; some of four jewels—gold, silver, lapis lazuli, and crystal; some of five jewels—gold, silver, lapis lazuli, crystal, and red pearls; some of six jewels—gold, silver, lapis lazuli, crystal, musaragalva, and red pearls; and some of seven jewels, up to and including agate.
Furthermore, it was adorned with red pearls, sandalwood, and blue lotuses (utpala), pink lotuses (padma), white lotuses (kumuda), and white water lilies (puṇḍarīka).

Furthermore, there rained down *sumanā* flowers, *campaka* flowers, *pāṭala* flowers, *atimuktaka* flowers, *raṇi* flowers, *kuraṇi* flowers, *māndārava* flowers, *mahāmāndārava* flowers, *pāruṣaka* flowers, *mahāpāruṣaka* flowers, *mañjūṣaka* flowers, *mahāmañjūṣaka* flowers, *rocanaka* flowers, *mahārocanaka* flowers, *cakra* flowers, *mahācakra* flowers, *suvicitracakra* flowers, *candana* flowers, *mahācandana* flowers, *suvicitracandanaka* flowers, *candanotara* flowers, *tāla* flowers, and *mahātāla* flowers. Upon those jeweled terraces, these various colors were variegated, brilliant, and pure, shining with radiant splendor.

Upon each of the jeweled terraces, there were eighty-four thousand transformed jade maidens, some holding kōnghóu lutes, qín and sè harps, zhēng and dí flutes, pípá lutes, drums, and conch shells; with such immeasurable musical instruments made of various jewels, they played subtle and wondrous sounds while standing in solemn stillness.
There were some jade maidens who held red candana sandalwood and agallocha candana sandalwood, or held black agallocha candana sandalwood, standing there with solemn composure.
Some jade maidens stood solemnly, holding *utpala*, *padma*, *kumuda*, and *puṇḍarīka* flowers.

Other jade maidens stood in majestic array, holding *māndārava*, *mahāmāndārava*, *pāruṣaka*, *mahāpāruṣaka*, *rocanaka*, *mahārocanaka*, *candana*, *mahācandana*, *sulocanacandana*, *cakraka*, *mahācakraka*, *sulocanacakraka*, *tāla*, *mahātāla*, and *sulocatāla* flowers.
There were also celestial maidens holding all kinds of flowers and fruits, standing there with solemn dignity.

Upon the various jeweled terraces were lion thrones adorned with many precious gems; upon each throne sat an emanation Buddha, his body naturally adorned with the thirty-two marks and eighty minor characteristics.
Upon each of the terraces hung eighty-four thousand strings of blue, yellow, red, and white mixed pearls, which were strung across the various jeweled terraces.
On each terrace were eighty-four thousand exquisite jeweled vases, filled to the brim with powdered incense and arranged in rows thereon.
Upon each of the jeweled terraces, there were eighty-four thousand exquisite canopies made of various jewels, completely covering them.
Upon each of the jeweled terraces, there were eighty-four thousand trees made of various jewels planted therein.
Upon each of the jeweled terraces, there were eighty-four thousand jeweled bells spread out and covering them.
Between the various jeweled trees were ponds made of the seven treasures, filled to the brim with water possessing the eight meritorious qualities.
There were lotuses made of various jewels—blue, yellow, red, and white—their radiant colors vivid and brilliant.
A gentle breeze stirred them, and from the rows of jewel-trees emerged subtle and wondrous sounds; these tones were harmonious and elegant, surpassing even the music of the heavens.
Upon each of the jeweled terraces, there were eighty-four thousand exquisite cords of various precious gems, stretching continuously between the trees.
Each and every jeweled terrace radiated light that illuminated eighty-four thousand yojanas, such that there was no place not brilliantly lit.

At that time, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas Avalokiteśvara and Mahāsthāmaprāpta, together with their retinues of eight thousand billion bodhisattvas, adorned with identical precious pavilions, vanished from that land and arrived in this world in the time it takes a strong man to bend and extend his arm.

At that time, by means of his supernormal powers, that bodhisattva caused the ground of this world to become as level as the surface of water. Surrounded before and behind by eight billion bodhisattvas, he was adorned with the perfection of great merit; he was so exceptionally handsome and sublime that nothing could serve as a comparison, and his radiance shone everywhere throughout the Sahā world.

These bodhisattvas approached the place where Śākyamuni Buddha was, prostrated themselves with their heads at his feet, circumambulated him seven times to the right, withdrew to stand to one side, and addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
"Amitābha Buddha sends his greetings to the World-Honored One: Are you free from illness and affliction? Is your daily life light and easy? Do you dwell in peace and happiness?

Furthermore, when the wondrous adornments of that land were manifested, these bodhisattvas and the assembly of śrāvakas, seeing this jeweled terrace with its manifold exquisite adornments, marveled at such an unprecedented sight and each thought to themselves:
"These jeweled terraces are so subtle and wonderful; have they come from the Land of Peace and Bliss to this world by the power of the Buddha?"
“Is it the power of a bodhisattva?
At that time, the Bodhisattva Flower-Virtue-Treasury (Kusumagarbha), sustained by the Buddha’s spiritual power, addressed the Buddha, saying:
“How extraordinary!
“World-Honored One!
This is unprecedented!
That this Sahā world is now adorned with such magnificent jeweled terraces—whose power is this?”
The Buddha said,
"This is through the power of the supernatural penetrations of Avalokiteśvara and Mahāsthāmaprāpta, who manifest great adornments in this world.
[The assembly exclaimed,] "How extraordinary!"
“World-Honored One!
This is inconceivable!
That son of good family, whose vows and practices are pure, is able to adorn this jeweled terrace with his supernormal powers and manifest it within this world.”
The Buddha said: "So it is! So it is!"
As you have said, that son of good family has, throughout countless hundreds of thousands of millions of nayutas of kalpas, purified all roots of goodness and attained the illusion-like samādhi.
Abiding in this samādhi, one can manifest such deeds through the transformations of supernatural powers.
Furthermore, Flower-Virtue-Treasury!
Observe now the world in the eastern direction; what do you see there?

At that time, Puṣpadharagarbha, by means of his various kinds of bodhisattva divine eyes, surveyed the Buddha-worlds in the eastern direction as numerous as the sands of the Ganges. He saw that before each of those Buddhas stood Avalokiteśvara and Mahāsthāmaprāpta, adorned as previously described, paying respectful offerings and all exclaiming:
“Amitābha Buddha inquires after the World-Honored One—whether he is free from illness and affliction, whether his daily life is light and easy, and whether he dwells in peace and happiness.”
“In the same way, it was so for the south, west, north, the four intermediate directions, and the zenith and nadir.
At that time, having witnessed this event, the Bodhisattva Padmaśrīgarbha was filled with joy and exultation; having attained what he had never experienced before, he addressed the Buddha, saying:
‘How extraordinary!’”
World-Honored One!
This Great Being is now able to accomplish such a samādhi.
For what reason?
"Now this true being is able to manifest the adornments of these buddha-fields.

At that time, the World-Honored One, by means of his supernatural power, caused the assembly to see this matter; thereupon, thirty-two thousand people resolved their minds upon *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
The Bodhisattva Guṇākara addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
How long ago did these two noble beings first resolve their minds toward anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi? Under which Buddha did they do so?”
"I only pray that you will explain this, so that all bodhisattvas may cultivate these vows and practices and achieve them in full perfection.
The Buddha said,
"Listen attentively!"
"Reflect upon this well; I shall speak for your sake.
"Excellent, World-Honored One!"
"I wish to hear it with joy.
The Buddha said,
"In the distant past, immeasurable, inconceivable, and incalculable *asaṃkhyeya* kalpas ago, at that time I was a king among hundreds of thousands of kings."

At that time, when the first great kalpa was nearing its end, there was a world named *Anantaguṇarāśisukhasaṃdarśana*. In that land there was a Buddha, titled *Suvarṇaprabhāsasiṃhavikrīḍita Tathāgata*, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Vidhyācaraṇasaṃpanna, Sugata, Lokavid, Anuttara, Puruṣadamyasārathi, Śāstā devamanuṣyāṇām, Buddha, Bhagavān. I shall now describe for you all the pure and magnificent adornments of that buddha-field.
"What do you think?
Is the extent of the adornments and purity of the land of Amitābha Buddha in the World of Peace and Bliss not great? He replied:
“Very much so!
It is inconceivable and difficult to describe in full.
The Buddha told Puṣpadharagarbha:
"Suppose there were a person who divided a single hair into a hundred hairs, and used one portion of those hairs to take up a drop of water from the great ocean. What do you think?
Between the water on the tip of that single hair and the water in the great ocean, which is more?"
He replied: "The waters of the ocean are so vast that they cannot serve as a simile.
"It is thus, Flower-Virtue-Treasury!"
One should understand it thus: the adornments of the land of Amitābha are like water on the tip of a hair;
the golden light and lion-play of the Buddha-land of the Buddha Suvarṇaprabhāsa-siṃhavikrīḍita are like the waters of the great ocean.
The distinction between śrāvakas and bodhisattvas is likewise the same.
That Tathāgata Golden Light Lion’s Play also expounds the Dharma of the Three Vehicles for the sake of sentient beings.

Even if I were to spend eons as numerous as the sands of the Ganges expounding upon the merits and adornments of this Buddha-land, and the matters of the bliss enjoyed by its bodhisattvas and śrāvakas, I could not exhaustively describe them.
At that time, within the Dharma of the Tathāgata Golden Light Lion’s Play, there was a king named King Majestic Virtue.
He ruled over a thousand worlds through the True Dharma and was known as a Dharma King.
That King Mahātejas had many sons, all of whom were endowed with the twenty-eight marks of a great man.
These princes all dwelt in the unsurpassed path.
The king possessed seventy-six thousand gardens and pavilions, wherein his sons played and sported.
Puṣpakuṭidhara addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!"
“Is there any woman in that Buddha-field? The Buddha said, “Good son!
In that Buddha-land, even the name "woman" does not exist, let alone a real one.
The sentient beings of that land purely cultivate the Brahma-faring; they are exclusively born by transformation and take the joy of dhyāna as their food.
For eighty-four billion years, that King Tejodhipati served the Tathāgata and practiced no other teaching.
Knowing his sincere resolve, the Buddha then expounded for him the Seal of the Infinite Dharma (Anantadharmamudrā).
What is the seal of the immeasurable Dharma?
Flower-Virtue-Treasury Bodhisattva!
In whatever practice one engages, one should give rise to immeasurable vows.

Why is this? Because for a bodhisattva-mahāsattva, there is immeasurable generosity, immeasurable morality, immeasurable patience, immeasurable diligence, immeasurable meditative concentration, and immeasurable wisdom; there is immeasurable engagement in the six perfections to encompass the cycle of birth and death, immeasurable compassion for sentient beings, immeasurable adornment of the pure land, immeasurable voice, and immeasurable eloquence.
Śrīgarbha! Even a single thought associated with virtue can be dedicated to the immeasurable.
How is it dedicated to the immeasurable?

To dedicate [merit] toward all sentient beings so that all sentient beings may attain the realization of non-arising and enter parinirvāṇa through the parinirvāṇa of the Buddha—this is called immeasurable dedication.

The immeasurability of infinite space, the immeasurability of signlessness, and the immeasurability of wishlessness; likewise, the absence of conditioned activity, the reality-limit of desirelessness, the non-arising of the nature of phenomena (*dharmatā*), unattached liberation, and the immeasurability of nirvāṇa.
"Good son! I have merely briefly explained that all dharmas are immeasurable. Why is this?
Because all phenomena are without limit.
Furthermore, Flower-Virtue-Treasury!
That King of Majestic Virtue entered into samādhi within his pleasure garden.
To the left and right of that king, two lotus flowers emerged from the earth, adorned with various colors and as fragrant as celestial sandalwood.
Within them, two youths were born by transformation, sitting cross-legged.
One was named Ratnamati and the other was named Ratnottama.
At that time, King Tejodhipati arose from his meditative concentration, saw the two youths seated within the Lotus Treasury, and addressed them with these verses:
"Are you gods, nāga kings, yakṣas, or kumbhāṇḍas?..."
"Are you a human or a non-human?
I pray that you will tell me your name.
Then, the youth on the king's right side replied in verse:
"All phenomena are empty; how can you ask for a name?
Past phenomena have already ceased, future phenomena have not yet arisen, and present phenomena do not abide.
Noble one, whose name are you asking about?"
"Empty phenomena are neither persons, nor are they nāgas or rākṣasas;
humans, non-humans, and so forth—all these are unobtainable.
Thus spoke the youth on the left in verse:
“Names and names are entirely empty; names and names cannot be apprehended.
All phenomena are nameless, yet you wish to inquire about names and seek a true name—something never before seen or heard.”
Since the nature of arising is itself cessation, why do you ask for a name?
To speak of names and words is entirely a matter of conventional designation;
my name is Ratnamati, and his name is Ratnottama.

“Puṣpālaṃkāragarbha! After these two youths had spoken this verse, they went together with King Tejodhipati to the place where the Buddha was. They prostrated themselves with their heads at his feet, circumambulated him seven times to the right, and stood to one side with palms joined in reverence.”
Then, the two youths together raised their voices and questioned the Buddha in verse:
"What constitutes true offering,
O Unsurpassed Honored One among Two-legged Beings?"
I pray that you will explain its meaning and intent, so that those who hear it may practice accordingly.
Among offerings such as flowers, incense, various musical performances, clothing, food, medicine, and bedding— which of these is the most supreme?
At that time, the Buddha spoke these verses for the youth:
"One should resolve to attain Bodhicitta, Universally delivering all living beings;
This is the true offering to the Perfectly Awakened One, Possessing the thirty-two marks of clarity."
Even if one were to fill worlds as numerous as the sands of the Ganges with exquisite and wondrous ornaments and offer them to all the Tathāgatas, who would joyfully receive and honor them,
it would not equal the merit of dedicating [merit] toward Bodhi with a mind of loving-kindness.
This merit is most supreme, immeasurable and boundless.
No other offering surpasses it; it exceeds all others beyond calculation.
Such a bodhicitta will surely bring about the attainment of perfect enlightenment.
Then the two youths spoke again in verse:
“O devas, nāgas, and spirits, listen to my lion’s roar!
Now, before the Tathāgata, I make a great vow and resolve for Bodhi.”
Throughout immeasurable kalpas of birth and death, the primordial limit is unknowable;
yet for the sake of a single sentient being, you have practiced the Way for that many kalpas.
How much more so during all these kalpas, as you deliver and liberate immeasurable multitudes!
While practicing the path to enlightenment, if weariness should arise in my mind,
and if from this moment forth I were to give rise to a heart of desire,
then I would be deceiving all the Buddhas of the ten directions.
The stains of anger and delusion, as well as stinginess and envy— now I speak words of truth, remaining far removed from all falsehood.
If, from this moment on, I were to give rise to the mind of a śrāvaka, [I would be a liar].
Those who do not delight in cultivating bodhi deceive the World-Honored One;
nor do they seek pratyekabuddhahood to save themselves and benefit their own bodies alone.
Rather, throughout ten billion kalpas, they shall use great compassion to deliver all sentient beings.
Just as this Buddha-field is now pure, wondrous, and magnificently adorned,
may it be when I attain the Way that it surpasses hundreds of thousands of millions [of such realms].
May there be no assembly of śrāvakas in that land, nor any of the pratyekabuddha vehicle.
There are bodhisattvas of pure existence, their number being limitless.
Sentient beings are purified and stainless, all fully possessing supreme and wondrous bliss;
they give birth to perfect awakening and master the treasury of all dharmas.
"If this vow is truthful, may the great trichiliocosm tremble.
Having spoken these verses, at that very moment the entire world shook violently,
and hundreds of thousands of musical instruments played forth harmonious and elegant sounds.
Radiant and exquisite robes swirl as he descends;
from amidst the sky, the various devas scatter a rain of powdered incense.
Its fragrance flows everywhere, perfuming all and gladdening the hearts of sentient beings.
The Buddha said to Puṣpacitra:
"What do you think? Was the King Tejodhipati at that time someone other than this person?"
I am that very person.
The two youths at that time were none other than the present Bodhisattva Mahāsattvas Avalokiteśvara and Mahāsthāmaprāpta.
O son of good family!
"These two bodhisattvas first resolved their minds toward *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* in the presence of that Buddha.
At that time, Puṣpākara-garbha addressed the Buddha, saying:
"How extraordinary!"
“World-Honored One!

This good man has never before resolved his mind [upon enlightenment], yet he has accomplished such profound wisdom as to thoroughly understand that all names and designations are ultimately unattainable.”
“World-Honored One!
Have these two noble men already made offerings to former Buddhas and performed various meritorious deeds?
“Good son! [The Buddha replied.]
The grains of sand in this Ganges River may all be counted, yet the roots of goodness planted by this Great Being through his prior offerings to the Buddhas are beyond calculation.
Although he has not yet resolved to attain Bodhicitta, he adorns himself with the inconceivable and is the most courageous among all sentient beings.
At that time, the Bodhisattva Puṣpadhvaja-garbha addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
In which direction lies that land called Anantaguṇasaṃcaya-sukhābhyudaya?”
The Buddha said:
"Good son! At that time, this Western World of Peace and Bliss shall be known as the Land of Peaceful Manifestation of the Accumulation of Immeasurable Virtues."
The Bodhisattva Puṣpadharagarbha addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
We pray that you will explain this for us, so that immeasurable sentient beings may obtain great benefit.”
In which land will this Avalokiteśvara attain equal and perfect enlightenment?

What will be the adornments of that world, its name, its radiance, and the number of its śrāvakas and bodhisattvas? What will be his lifespan, and what will be the circumstances of his attainment of Buddhahood?
If the World-Honored One were to speak of the vows previously practiced by this bodhisattva, other bodhisattvas, having heard these vows, would surely practice them and attain fulfillment.
The Buddha said:
“Excellent! Listen attentively!”
"I shall explain it for you. He replied,
"Yes, indeed!"
"I wish to hear it with joy. The Buddha said, "Good son!
The lifespan of Amitābha Buddha is immeasurable hundreds of thousands of billions of kalpas, yet it shall eventually come to an end. Good son!
In the distant future, after incalculable kalpas, Amitābha Buddha shall enter parinirvāṇa.
After his parinirvāṇa, the True Dharma shall remain in the world for a duration equal to the Buddha’s lifespan.
Whether during his lifetime or after his passing, all those beings he delivers shall be exactly equal.
After the Buddha’s nirvāṇa, there may be sentient beings who do not see the Buddha; yet there are bodhisattvas who, having attained the buddhānusmṛti-samādhi, constantly behold Amitābha Buddha.
Furthermore, good son!
After that Buddha’s parinirvāṇa, all the precious bathing pools, lotus flowers, and rows of jewel-trees will constantly emanate the sound of the Dharma, no different from that of the Buddha himself.

"Good son! After the True Dharma of Amitābha Buddha has perished, at the time when the clear signs of dawn appear after midnight, the Bodhisattva Avalokiteśvara shall sit cross-legged beneath a bodhi tree made of the seven precious substances and attain equal and perfect enlightenment, receiving the name Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Vidya-caraṇa-saṃpanna, Sugata, Lokavid, Anuttara, Puruṣadamyasārathi, Śāstā devamanuṣyāṇām, Buddha, Bhagavān, named Universal Radiance Mountain King of Merit."
That Buddha-land is composed of the seven treasures appearing spontaneously, adorned with a multitude of exquisite and harmonious embellishments.
Even if all the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, were to speak for kalpas as numerous as the sands of the Ganges, they could not exhaustively describe them.

"Good son! I shall now speak a parable for you regarding the adornments of the land of the Tathāgata Golden Light Lion’s Play. Compared to the land of the Tathāgata Universal Radiance Mountain King of Merit, it exceeds it by a hundred thousand million times, a billion times, ten trillion times, and even beyond what can be reached by calculation."
"In that Buddha-land, there is no mention of the names 'śrāvaka' or 'pratyekabuddha'; it is filled exclusively with bodhisattvas.
The Bodhisattva Puṣpadhvaja-garbha addressed the Buddha, saying, "World-Honored One!"
“Is that Buddha-land named ‘Peaceful Bliss’?
The Buddha said, “Good son!...”
That Buddha-land is named Universal Array of All Jewels.
Good son! The Tathāgata Universal Radiance Merit Mountain King [remains] for the duration of his lifespan.
The Bodhisattva Mahāsthāmaprāpta personally attended upon and made offerings to him until his parinirvāṇa.
After his parinirvāṇa, he upheld the True Dharma until its ultimate extinction.

When the Dharma has completely vanished, he shall immediately attain anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi in that very land, receiving the title Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, Vidya-caraṇa-saṃpanna, Sugata, Lokavid, Anuttara, Puruṣadamyasārathi, Śāstā devamanuṣyāṇām, Buddha, Bhagavān, named Guṇaratnarāja-suvyūha.
It shall be no different from the land of the Tathāgata Universal Radiance Mountain King of Merit, nor his radiance, lifespan, assembly of bodhisattvas, nor even the duration of the Dharma.
If any son or daughter of good family hears the name of the Tathāgata Jewel King of Well-Abiding Merit, they shall all attain non-retrogression from *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*.
Furthermore, noble son!

If there are women who hear the names of the Tathāgata Past Golden Light Lion’s Play and the Tathāgata Well-Abiding Jewel-King of Merit, they shall all transform their female bodies and eliminate the offenses of birth and death for forty billion kalpas. They shall all become non-retrogressive regarding *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, constantly behold the Buddhas, hear and receive the True Dharma, and make offerings to the Saṅgha.
After casting off this body, they shall leave the household life and achieve unimpeded eloquence, swiftly attaining *dhāraṇī*.
At that time, six billion beings within the assembly raised their voices in unison, exclaiming:
"Namo to the Buddhas of the ten directions who have entered parinirvāṇa!
With one mind, they deliberated together and resolved to attain anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
The Buddha then bestowed upon him the prediction that he would attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
Furthermore, eighty-four thousand nayutas of sentient beings were distanced from dust and freed from defilement, attaining the pure Dharma-eye regarding all phenomena.
Seven thousand bhikṣus attained the exhaustion of outflows and liberation of mind.

At that time, the Bodhisattvas Avalokiteśvara and Mahāsthāmaprāpta, by means of their supernatural powers, caused this entire assembly to see the countless Buddhas, World-Honored Ones, of the ten directions, all of whom were bestowing upon them the prediction of Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.
Having seen this, he exclaimed:
"How extraordinary!
World-Honored One!"
"These Tathāgatas have bestowed such a prophecy upon this Great Being!
At that time, the Bodhisattva Puṣpākara-garbha addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!..."

If a son of good family or a daughter of good family were to receive, uphold, read, recite, explain, transcribe, and widely propagate this profound sūtra of the Tathāgata, how much merit would they obtain?
I only pray that the Tathāgata will analyze and explain this. Why is this?

In the evil world of the future, sentient beings of meager merit will not believe or accept these profound sūtras of the Tathāgata; for this reason, they will suffer for a long night and find it difficult to attain liberation.
World-Honored One!
We only pray that you will speak of it, out of compassion and for the benefit of all sentient beings.
World-Honored One!
"In this assembly today, there are many sons and daughters of good family with sharp faculties who will become great luminaries in future ages.
The Buddha said,
"Flower-Virtue-Treasury!"
"Excellent! Listen attentively;
I shall speak for you. He replied:
“Please accept our instruction!
We wish most earnestly to hear it.
The Buddha said:

"If a good son were to place all sentient beings of the trichiliocosm upon his two shoulders and, for the remainder of their lives, provide them with whatever they required and desired—food, clothing, bedding, mattresses, and medicinal decoctions—would the merit he thereby obtained be great?"
“Very much, World-Honored One!
If one were to provide for a single sentient being with a mind of loving-kindness according to their needs, the merit would be immeasurable; how much more so for all beings!”
The Buddha said:

“If a son of good family or a daughter of good family receives, maintains, reads, recites, explains, transcribes, makes various offerings to, and widely propagates this sutra, and gives rise to the bodhicitta, the merit they obtain shall be hundreds of thousands of millions of times beyond comparison.”
The Bodhisattva Puṣpadharagarbha addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

From this day forward, regarding these sutras spoken by the Tathāgata, as well as the names of the three Buddhas of the past and the future, I shall constantly receive, uphold, read, recite, explain, copy, and widely propagate them. I shall remain far removed from the minds of greed, anger, and delusion, resolve for *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi*, and never again act with falsehood.”
"Blessed One!
When I attain Buddhahood, if there are women who hear such a Dharma as this, may they immediately transform their female bodies;
having transformed their female bodies, I shall grant them the prediction that they will attain Anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, and they shall be named Vimala Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyak-saṃbuddha."

When this sutra had been spoken, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Padmaśrīgarbha, along with the bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, bodhisattvas, śrāvakas, devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, humans, non-humans, and others, having heard what the Buddha had taught, were all greatly rejoiced.
The Sūtra on the Prophecy of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva’s Attainment of Buddhahood.
